3.q: Trace the correct sequence of effects by which the Napoleonic Code in the Grand Duchy of Warsaw both advanced and limited Polish national hopes.
3.a: The dual legacy runs: (1) The Code abolishes serfdom and builds a merit-based bureaucracy (2) A shared legal framework fosters a common Polish civic identity (3) French courts impose the French language and military conscription follows (4) Ultimate sovereignty stays with Napoleon and caps Polish liberty. A wrong answer that lists only benefits, or only impositions, shows the student has missed the dual legacy in which the very laws that advanced Polish nationhood also limited it.

5.q: Give the correct sequence of legacies by which the Carbonari, though suppressed, shaped the Risorgimento after 1821.
5.a: The legacy chain runs: (1) Repression after the Congress of Vienna drives patriots into secret societies (2) The Carbonari keep the tricolour, the constitution and the idea of Italy alive underground (3) The 1820 to 1821 uprisings force monarchs to concede constitutions and prove pressure works (4) Survivors like Mazzini convert conspiracy into the mass moral mission of Young Italy. A wrong answer that calls the societies irrelevant failures shows the student has missed that they trained the generation of 1848 and kept nationalism alive when open politics was impossible.

6.q: Trace the correct sequence of design choices for building a national allegory for newly independent India in 1947.
6.a: The design sequence runs: (1) Choose the motherland figure of the Bharat Mata tradition as the base (2) Give her the charkha for self-reliance and the Ashoka Chakra for dharma and continuity (3) Add a tricolour sash for unity in diversity (4) Omit every imperial icon of British rule and display the image in schools and town halls where Marianne and Germania were shown. A wrong answer that copies a crown or a conquering sword from European models shows the student has missed that each attribute must carry the new nation's own meanings of fearlessness, labour and unity.
